question: Will a US governor, congressperson or cabinet member formally declare a 2028 presidential run before 2027?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: open-field out-party presidential cycles (2004, 2008, 2012R, 2016R, 2020, 2024R). In about half, a sitting official filed with the FEC in Nov-Dec of the midterm year (Kerry Dec 2002, Kucinich/Vilsack 2006, Warren Dec 31 2018). As of Nov 23, 2026 no officeholder has filed. Main paths: Beshear, who said he'd decide after his DGA chair ends in December (CNN reported a possible December launch; his PAC adviser called it 'categorically false'), and Khanna, who will decide 'over the holidays'. Most others point to the new year. The Polymarket 'announce before 2027' market (~$1.48M volume) implies about 50% combined for officeholders, but it counts announcements rather than Form 2 filings and its thin long-shot prices (Warnock 24% on $6k) run high, so I discount it.
calls.reference_class: Open-nomination out-party presidential cycles 2004-2024: whether a sitting governor/member of Congress/cabinet member filed FEC Form 2 before Jan 1 of the year before the election

calls.reasoning: Status quo as of Nov 23, 2026: no sitting governor, member of Congress or cabinet member has declared or filed FEC Form 2 for 2028; the declared candidates are minor figures who hold no office. About five weeks remain, including the holidays. Base rate: in cycles 2004-2024, 3 of 6 had a sitting official file before the year-before-election (Dean 2002, Vilsack Nov 2006, Delaney 2017), but those filings came earlier or were already visible by late November; the conditional rate for a filing in the last five weeks with nothing visible yet is closer to 10-15%. The main path is Gov. Beshear: CNN reported in October a possible launch after the December DGA meeting, his ex-campaign manager called it 'not true', Beshear says he has 'no timetable', and Kalshi gives him about 7% to be the first Democrat to announce. Khanna will decide over the holidays, pointing to January; Bacon is only considering and leaves office Jan 3; DeSantis and Newsom point to early 2027. Markets: Kalshi has per-person announcement markets with 2027 deadlines (Mar-Jul), not this contract, so they are indirect evidence only; Kalshi pages were rate-limited, so prices, volume and recent moves come from search snippets and media reports. Polymarket and Manifold: no matching market found.

calls.reference_class: Open-seat presidential cycles 2004-2024: whether a sitting governor/member of Congress/cabinet member filed FEC Form 2 before Jan 1 of the year before the election (and specifically in the final ~5 weeks)

calls.reasoning: As of 2026-11-24 no sitting governor/member of Congress/cabinet member has filed Form 2 for 2028; only minor non-officeholders (Greaney, Royce White) have declared. Base rate: in roughly 2 of 6 recent post-midterm late-Nov-to-Dec windows a sitting officeholder filed (Kucinich Dec 2006, Warren Dec 31 2018), mostly in open crowded fields like this one. Main live paths: Beshear (CNN reported a possible launch after the December DGA meeting; denied by his former campaign manager), Kelly (staffing up), Khanna (draft committee, deciding over the holidays), Bacon (retiring, weighing a run). Most contenders (Newsom early Jan, Vance 2027, Emanuel new year, Slotkin within six months) point to 2027. Polymarket 'announce before 2027' (announcement, not Form 2; thin, longshot-biased) sums to ~35-40% across officeholders; discounted for longshot bias and the Form 2 requirement.
calls.reference_class: Post-midterm Nov 24-Dec 31 windows in open or semi-open presidential cycles (2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022): did a sitting governor/member of Congress/cabinet member file Form 2?
